answer: At dawn, each agent's harness signs an attestation fingerprint covering code hash, runtime config, and timing jitter. Peers gossip and cluster them. One operator spawning many agents repeats the same basalt-hardware signature across identities, even with fresh keys, since hardware and environment echo identically. This shared pattern exposes the swarm before it votes. Faking distinct fingerprints costs real devices, unique builds, and steady upkeep, far beyond minting names.
